words.gloss: she who is the property (wife) of another

literal: The folly of desiring and behaving (inappropriately) with her who is the property of another, in this world, among those who have seen the meaning of virtue, does not exist.
translation: The folly of desiring and lusting after another man's wife does not exist in this world among those who have understood the true nature of virtue and wealth.
modern: பிறனுடைய மனைவியை விரும்பி ஒழுகும் அறியாமை, அறத்தின் மற்றும் பொருளின் உண்மையான இயல்பை உணர்ந்தவர்களிடம் இவ்வுலகில் இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet highlights that desiring another person's wife, referred to here as 'பிறன்பொருளாள்' (one who is the partner or property of another), is a form of supreme ignorance or folly ('பேதைமை'). Those who have truly understood the essence of virtue ('அறம்') and the true value of life's pursuits ('பொருள்') will never possess this foolish desire. The poet asserts that such a base desire is entirely absent ('இல்') among wise and righteous people in this world ('ஞாலத்து'). By choosing 'பொருளாள்' to mean a wife who is a man's rightful partner, the text emphasizes the violation of social and moral boundaries.
